newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: NEW ARGENTINE ALLIANCE WANTS 10 PCT BASIC VAT.
newsitem.headline: NEW ARGENTINE ALLIANCE WANTS 10 PCT BASIC VAT.

text.p: Argentina's new opposition alliance said Sunday it would like to see value added tax on essential goods slashed to 10 percent from its current 21 percent.

Carlos Alvarez of the centre-left coalition Frepaso, which has teamed up with the centrist Radical Party for elections for Congress in October, told supporters at a weekend rally in the province of La Pampa that the alliance was "seriously studying changes in the tax system."

"Argentina has one of the most backward tax systems in the world and VAT is one of the highest in the world. We propose reducing it to 10 percent for essential goods in order to increase consumption and improve the distribution of income," said Alvarez, a national deputy for the Frepaso.
The new alliance burst upon the political scene a week ago, dramatically altering the panorama for October's vote and for presidential elections in 1999.
Peronist President Carlos Menem has counterattacked by charging that the alliance would return Argentina to the economic chaos of the late 1980s, when the Radicals governed under Raul Alfonsin.

The Frepaso and Radical leaders have stressed they would not touch "convertibility" -- the peso/dollar parity in place since 1991, which is credited with beating Argentine inflation to zero and bringing economic stability.

Alvarez said the alliance "will defend Convertibility, fiscal balance and a competitive economy open to the world. We would not go back on privatisations, because we cannot undermine confidence in our country's laws."
But the alliance has given support, albeit lukewarm, to a general strike planned for August 14 by dissident trade unions against high unemployment and labour law reforms planned by Menem.
